messages:
aisha: hey team — first day, trying to kick off the pipeline for my repo (redwood/api-sdk) but it bails immediately. Buildkite shows a 403 when the job starts and the GHA runner can't fetch the docker image. not sure who to ping for perms

ci-bot: Pipeline created: redwood/api-sdk #1 — triggered by aisha :rocket:

ben: welcome aboard! quick checks: did you accept the org invite? also are you using oauth or a PAT for Buildkite? sometimes people miss the pipeline team access. can you paste the small error output?

aisha: I accepted the org invite and can see the repo. `bk login` completed, but `bk agents` returns empty. here's the Buildkite agent error from the job log:

```
2024-07-08T10:02:13Z ERROR starting job: agent denied: 403 Forbidden - invalid agent token
```

and when the job tries to pull the image from GHCR: `docker pull ghcr.io/redwood/inference:latest` -> `Error response from daemon: pull access denied for ghcr.io/redwood/inference, repository does not exist or may require 'docker login'`

lina: two likely things: 1) GH App installation / org membership — GHCR often needs a PAT with read:packages or the GH App to be installed on the repo/org. 2) Buildkite needs you to be added to the pipeline/team (or the agent token to be present on the host). For GHCR try:

```bash
echo "$GITHUB_PAT" | docker login ghcr.io -u YOUR_USERNAME --password-stdin
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_PAT" https://ghcr.io/v2/redwood/inference/manifests/latest
```

oncall-sre: also if you're on the k8s ephemeral agents path, check the k8s cluster is running agents and the `BK_AGENT_TOKEN` secret is configured in the agent deployment. if using self-hosted agent, ensure `/etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg` has a valid token. post the short outputs and we can point to the exact missing bit.

aisha: ran the curl check and got:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Server: GitHub.com
```

so PAT isn't authorizing me for GHCR. i created a PAT quickly from github.com with `read:packages` and `repo` scopes but still 401.

ben: aha — two possibilities: the PAT you created needs to be from a user that has access to that package (if the package is private). also org SSO can block PAT usage until you approve it. go to https://github.com/organizations/redwood/settings/installations to confirm the GitHub App is installed for the repo, and Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Authorized OAuth Apps / SSO to ensure PAT is allowed. i've added you to the redwood/api-sdk pipeline team — try re-triggering the job.

ci-bot: Buildkite: job #1 retried by ben — started

aisha: great — job just progressed to setup and started pulling images, looks like the permissions change fixed it. thanks! :tada:

lina: fyi for the onboarding doc we recommend:
- If you need GHCR in CI and the package is private, either 1) use the org-installed GH App + pipeline-level token, or 2) create a PAT with `read:packages` and ensure SSO approval.
- For Buildkite agents: either use the org-managed ephemeral agents (k8s) or add your user to the pipeline/team and make sure agents have a valid `BK_AGENT_TOKEN`.

ben: i'll add a small blurb to the new-hire CI checklist about GHCR vs GH App and the common SSO gotcha. also note: if you're running a local self-hosted agent, the token in `/etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg` must match the token in the pipeline settings.

aisha: thanks everyone — this was super fast. tagging this thread for future new-hire notes. @ben can you add the GHCR/SSO note to the onboarding doc?

ben: yep i'll update the doc and leave a short how-to on creating an organization-approved PAT + docker login example. done.

aisha: awesome — first build green. feeling less new already :grin:
